takeaways.title: Chat cost chip for the assistant
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui/assistant`, you can now import `AssistantChatCost` to show what an open chat has cost so far, as the amount charged on credits or on the person's own key.

takeaways.title: Cost shows in the `LumenAssistant` header
takeaways.body: `LumenAssistant` now renders `AssistantChatCost` in its header, left of the chats (history) picker, so you get the cost chip with no extra props. It reads ≈ when the chat's plan sign-in calls at API rates are included in the amount.

takeaways.title: Hover to see where the cost came from
takeaways.body: Hovering the `AssistantChatCost` chip splits the amount into key, credits, and plan calls ≈ at API rates (charged $0). It reads the existing usage history entry `chat:<id>`, so you need no new endpoint, and the chip is hidden until the chat has a history line.

takeaways.title: Plan calls are priced from stored tokens
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ops, `usage()` now returns each entry with its plan-call cost recalculated from the tokens stored on that entry, so `own_plan_usd` no longer under-reports.

takeaways.title: Older chats get a real plan cost
takeaways.body: Chats that started before plan pricing was recorded now show a priced total from `usage()` for their later turns, not just the old estimate.

takeaways.title: The higher figure wins
takeaways.body: The new `withPlanUsd` step prices an entry's stored $0 parts at API rates and keeps that figure only when it is larger than the stored `own_plan_usd`, so existing totals are never lowered.

takeaways.title: Web tools no longer vanish when the lookup service is unreachable
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ai, turning on the `web.lookup` option while the lookup service has no service binding and no saved access token now falls back to the plain `fetch` web tool, so the assistant can still browse instead of asking the person.

takeaways.title: Lookup rules only appear when lookup is really available
takeaways.body: The lookup rules line is now added to the prompt only when `web__lookup` is among the turn's tools, as reported by the `lookup` field on `ToolsSummary`, so the assistant is never told about a tool it doesn't have.

takeaways.title: Word each tool call from its own arguments and answer
takeaways.body: In `LumenAgent`, the new protected `stepLine(c: StepCall)` method lets an app return a line such as "Editing Lid", "Edited Lid: wall 2 → 3 mm" or "Couldn't edit Lid" from `c.state` (`running`, `done` or `failed`), `c.input` and `c.output`, or return `undefined` to keep the tool's title.

takeaways.title: Live tool lines update in place
takeaways.body: `useAssistantChat` now updates a running line in place when a second `step_start` with the same id arrives once the arguments are in, and finished lines are saved with the chat as `line:<call id>`, so a chat read back shows the same words.

takeaways.title: Web lookups say what they looked up
takeaways.body: The kit's own web lookup now reads "Looking up <question>" while it runs and "Couldn't look up <question>" on failure, and a finished lookup keeps its web card.

takeaways.title: No more "Look something up" line for tool search
takeaways.body: In a plain chat (`plainSteps()`), the tool search that turns on more tools no longer shows a line, so people only see steps the assistant took for them.

takeaways.title: Plan sign-in calls now show an API-rate estimate
takeaways.body: In `OwnKeyUsage` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, a plan sign-in's calls no longer read $0, and each session and the "Earlier, plan" row show the key cost plus the plan calls priced at the model's API rates, marked ≈.

takeaways.title: Price token usage at API rates
takeaways.body: From @columenlabs/lumen-ai `state`, the new `listUsd(part)` returns a part's cost at the model's API rates (cache writes count as plain input), and `ownPlanUsd(paying, parts)` totals the plan-covered portion.

takeaways.title: Spend rows and usage entries carry the estimate
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ai, `withProvider` now adds `list_usd` to every $0 row that has calls, and `addUsage` stores `own_plan_usd` on the chat or run entry.

takeaways.title: Optional estimate fields in the view model types
takeaways.body: @columenlabs/lumen-ui-types adds `SpendState.rows[].list_usd?` and `UsageEntry.own_plan_usd?`, so existing code keeps compiling and you can read the estimate where you need it.

takeaways.title: Web lookup subagent
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/subagents`, `webLookupTools(source, { pages, answerTokens, blockHosts })` gives your assistant one `web__lookup` tool that answers a question from the web and returns about 1k tokens of `{ question, sources: [{ url, title, answer }], failed }` instead of whole pages.

takeaways.title: One-switch web mode in the engine
takeaways.body: In the engine options, the new `web.lookup` option (`true` or an options object) swaps the web tool group for just `web__lookup`, with its own rule about citing sources, so the assistant no longer sees raw fetch or scraping tools.

takeaways.title: Lookups show up in the panel
takeaways.body: `StepWeb` now has optional `lookup` and `reads` fields, filled in by `webStep`, so the panel shows "Looked up: …  N sources", folds the pages beneath it, and numbers them as Sources chips.

takeaways.title: Plan sign-in calls show up in Spent on your keys
takeaways.body: In `OwnKeyUsage` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, each chat or run answered through a person's plan sign-in now gets its own row at $0, with the plan and call count in its name.

takeaways.title: Usage entries count plan calls
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ai, usage entries now keep `own_plan_calls` (filled through `ownPlanCalls`) next to `own_usd`, so you can see how many calls a plan sign-in answered.

takeaways.title: Earlier plan calls are grouped into one row
takeaways.body: `OwnKeyUsage` now shows plan calls that no entry carries as a single "Earlier" row with the call count, so the total still adds up.

takeaways.title: Optional field on `UsageEntry`
takeaways.body: From @columenlabs/lumen-ui-types, `UsageEntry` has a new optional `own_plan_calls` field. It is additive, so existing code keeps compiling.

takeaways.title: Hand-offs work on a plan sign-in
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `planFetch` now sends every model call as streamed and turns the events back into the single JSON response your code expects, so the `escalate` tool ("Take a closer look") no longer fails with `400 Stream must be set to true`.

takeaways.title: Compaction works on a plan sign-in
takeaways.body: `LumenAgent` compaction makes calls that aren't streamed, and because they now go through `planFetch` they succeed instead of failing with the same 400.

takeaways.title: Hand-offs have a time limit
takeaways.body: The `escalate` tool in `@columenlabs/lumen-ai` now gives up after `HAND_OFF_MS` (240 s, newly exported), so a chat turn can no longer wait on a hand-off forever.

takeaways.title: Single-select `Select` marks the picked row with a fill, not a check
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `SelectItem` no longer renders a check mark, and the picked row gets a muted background (the same fill `DropdownMenuRadioItem` uses), so a single-select `Select` needs no changes in your app beyond expecting the new look.

takeaways.title: `Combobox` shows checks only when `multiple`
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `ComboboxItem` now highlights the picked row with a muted fill and draws the check only inside a list with `aria-multiselectable="true"`, which `ComboboxList` sets when you pass `multiple`.

takeaways.title: One rule for check marks across pickers
takeaways.body: A check box or check mark now appears only on multi-select pickers, and `LumenSelector` already follows this by drawing its box only when `multiple` is set, so it behaves the same as before.

takeaways.title: Plain tool lines in the assistant chat
takeaways.body: Call `LumenAgent.plainSteps()` in `@columenlabs/lumen-ai` to turn on plain mode, which shows friendly wording for tool lines, hides row counts, says "didn't work" for failures, and labels hand-offs "Take a closer look" with no tier or task.

takeaways.title: Tool titles on chat lines
takeaways.body: A chat line now shows the tool's own `ToolInfo.title` (from an MCP or plain tool), the titles are saved with the chat so a reloaded chat reads the same, and tools without a title still show their name.

takeaways.title: Failed calls go to your logs
takeaways.body: `LumenAgent.stepFailed({ tool, error, ms })` is called for every failed tool call with the whole error, so you can keep raw errors off the screen and in your logs.

takeaways.title: More detail in `called` and `onStep`
takeaways.body: Both now carry `error` and `caller`, and a failed `escalate` reports its raw error through `onStep` with `handoff: true`.

takeaways.title: Cleaner hand-off sections in the chat UI
takeaways.body: The chat hides a hand-off section's task when it is empty, and Copy chat leaves it out too.

takeaways.title: Know when a running tool is writing
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `chunkEvents` now sets `write: true` on `step_start` for write tools, and in `useAssistantChat` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ui` the running `LiveItem` carries `writing`, so your app can stop showing a pending change as ready while the assistant is still rewriting it.

takeaways.title: Own cap counts only API-key spend
takeaways.body: In the `@columenlabs/lumen-ai` `State`, the own cap (`paying`, via `ownCapUsed`) now counts only spend paid by an API key on a provider the person can still pay with, and plan sign-in calls count $0.

takeaways.title: Cap meter fits its row
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `ShareMeter` with `capped` no longer renders the spill slot, so the bar stops at its percentage and the amount sits on the line below.

takeaways.title: Clearer own-key usage
takeaways.body: `OwnKeyUsage` in `@columenlabs/lumen-ui` now leaves plan rows out and lists spend on a provider that is no longer usable as its own row, "Key not in use now, not counted".

takeaways.title: Long messages no longer run under the chat tools
takeaways.body: In `LumenComposer` (used inside `LumenAssistant` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui), text that grows until the box scrolls now stays clear of the paperclip, image icons and send button, so the last line is always readable.

takeaways.title: Chat tools sit on their own row
takeaways.body: In `LumenComposer`, the paperclip, the `modes` toggles and Send/Stop/Queue now share one row under the text, with no prop changes needed in your app.

takeaways.title: One border and focus ring around text and tools
takeaways.body: `LumenComposer` is now built from the kit's `InputGroup` with `InputGroupTextarea` and `InputGroupAddon align="block-end"` instead of a `Textarea` with floating tools, so apps get the fix by upgrading @columenlabs/lumen-ui.

takeaways.title: Pick who pays first with a segmented control
takeaways.body: In the assistant settings in `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the **Answers run on** setting is now a two-option `ToggleGroup` ("Your own first" | "Credits first") in place of the `LumenSelector`, so users see both choices at once and use the same control as the 1d/7d/30d range.

takeaways.title: No more letter box on provider rows
takeaways.body: In the assistant settings in `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, provider rows for your own and shared keys no longer draw the `ConnectionLogo` letter fallback (`text`), so each row starts with the provider name.

takeaways.title: Mount ⌘K Find on any screen
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenFinder` is now exported, so an app that draws its own frame (a full-screen editor with no `LumenShell`) can wrap its screen in `LumenFinder` to get the ⌘K Find dialog.

takeaways.title: Add your own Find commands outside the shell
takeaways.body: Inside `LumenFinder`, `useLumenFinderRows` lets you register rows with a `run` callback, for example a command that switches between mouse and trackpad navigation.

takeaways.title: Find no longer needs a router
takeaways.body: `LumenFinder` now works in an app with no router, where each row either calls its `run` function or follows a plain link, and inside `LumenShell` nothing changes.

takeaways.title: Know who paid for an AI answer
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ai, `Assistant.complete()` now also returns `payer` (`app` or `own`), so an app can show cost on the person's own key as money and everything else as credits.

takeaways.title: See the monthly cap being used
takeaways.body: In the own-AI section of assistant settings (Providers), a new "Used this month" row, built from `SettingField` and `ShareMeter`, shows spend against the person's monthly cap, for example "$30.06 of $30".

takeaways.title: Earlier spend no longer shows as "Nothing spent"
takeaways.body: In `OwnKeyUsage` ("Spent on your keys"), this month's own spend that no chat carries now appears as an "Earlier this month, not per chat" row, even when the cap is already full.

takeaways.title: Free rows are typed
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ui-types, `SpendState.rows` and `UsageHistory.rows` now declare `free?: true`, so you can read the flag the engine already sends. Free rows count toward neither the used nor the cap number.

takeaways.title: Settings controls line up on the right
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, every `SettingField` row now puts its label on the left and its control flush to the right edge, so you no longer need per-field spacing tweaks to align a Settings section.

takeaways.title: Stacked rows keep their control on the left on phones
takeaways.body: When you use `SettingField` with the `stack` layout on a phone-width screen, the control stays at the left under its label instead of jumping to the right edge.

takeaways.title: Label column unchanged
takeaways.body: `SettingField` labels keep the uncut label column from the previous release, so right-aligning the control does not clip or shift your label text.

takeaways.title: Keep a tier off people's allowance
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, the new `AssistantOptions.credits` option takes `(tier) => boolean`, and when it returns false for a tier, that tier's `complete()` and `agentTurn()` calls run on the app's key and are never stopped at `app_cap`.

takeaways.title: Free-tier spend stays visible but uncounted
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, spend from a tier where `credits` returns false is recorded as `SpendRow.free`, so you can still see it while it is left out of `appBudget` and the payer sums.

takeaways.title: No false "out of allowance" banner
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `status` now works out `wait` with the main tier's rules, so a free tier no longer shows an "out of allowance" banner.

takeaways.title: Long SettingField labels are no longer cut on desktop
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the `SettingField` label column still starts at 8rem but now widens to fit a longer name, so you no longer need to shorten or rename labels to avoid a trailing "…".

takeaways.title: SettingField labels wrap on a phone
takeaways.body: On a phone, `SettingField` now caps the label column at half the row and wraps longer labels onto more lines instead of cutting them. The column still starts at 6rem.

takeaways.title: Short labels still line up, with no per-label tuning
takeaways.body: `SettingField` sizes the label column automatically, so rows with short labels stay aligned and you pass no new prop or width.

takeaways.title: A lone admin now shows up in the People list
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenPeople` now shows its first-run note ("It's just you so far") only when `people` is empty, so an app with a single admin gets a table with that one row instead.

takeaways.title: "Not set up" no longer reads as a failed sync
takeaways.body: In `LumenPeople`, the sign-in sync tile and the person drawer now show "Not set up" when `sync.configured` is `false`, instead of a red "Out of step".

takeaways.title: Clearer sync states
takeaways.body: `LumenPeople` now reads Not set up, Synced or Out of step, and red is kept for a configured sync that failed, so you can tell a missing setup from a real failure.

takeaways.title: Every Settings row is now a `SettingField`
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the rows in `assistantSettingsSections` (your own keys, tier, models, tools, web, spend, allowance), `OwnKeyUsage`, General (Appearance and Preferences) and `LumenSecurity` all use `SettingField`, so a settings screen has one row layout.

takeaways.title: `SettingRow` is deprecated
takeaways.body: `SettingRow` now renders a `SettingField` and maps its `description` prop to `info`, so existing apps still build, but you should switch to `SettingField` and `info`.

takeaways.title: Settings search lives in `SettingField`
takeaways.body: Through the `SettingsSearch` context, any `SettingField` you place in a settings screen is now found by settings search, with no separate row component needed.

takeaways.title: The assistant's screen tool finds rows by `setting-field`
takeaways.body: The assistant now locates settings rows by their `setting-field` slot, because the old `setting-row` slot is no longer drawn. If your own code or tests select `data-slot="setting-row"`, change them to `setting-field`.

takeaways.title: Own keys only show ways the app allows
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the Model providers section of `assistantSettingsSections` (`Providers` and `OwnProviderKey`) now shows a provider row, a key way or a plan way only when the app's `ownWays` (status `own_ways`) allows it, so a person no longer sees a key marked "Works" that the server will not use.

takeaways.title: Summary lines follow the app's allowed ways
takeaways.body: In the same section, "Answers run on" and "Your keys may spend" now appear only when a way the app allows is set.

takeaways.title: Disallowed keys are hidden, not removed
takeaways.body: A stored key or sign-in the app does not allow stays saved but hidden and unused, and it shows again if you later allow that way in `ownWays`. Apps that leave out `own_ways` see no change.

takeaways.title: See what your own key or plan paid, per session
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the new `OwnKeyUsage` component appears at the end of the Providers section in Settings ▸ Model providers, so a person who brings their own key or plan can see what it paid for each session, with a Total row and a 1d / 7d / 30d range.

takeaways.title: Record own-key spend as you track usage
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `State.addUsage` now takes `own_usd` and adds it to the session's entry, so your engine can record how much of each session's cost the person's own key or plan paid.

takeaways.title: Own-key share on usage entries
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types`, `UsageEntry` has a new optional `own_usd` field holding the part of `usd` that the person's own key or plan paid, so your views can show it next to total spend.

takeaways.title: Access key fetch no longer hangs requests
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-auth`, `AccessVerifier` now gives up fetching its signing keys after `ACCESS_CERTS_MS` (3 seconds, exported), so a stalled key endpoint can no longer leave your routes waiting until the browser times out.

takeaways.title: One shared key fetch at a time
takeaways.body: `AccessVerifier` now runs a single key fetch at once and every request that needs keys waits on that one, so a slow endpoint no longer piles up unbounded fetches.

takeaways.title: Held keys keep verifying during a refresh
takeaways.body: Once the cached keys in `AccessVerifier` are past an hour old, they keep verifying tokens while fresh keys load in the background, so sign-in checks no longer wait on the refetch.

takeaways.title: Unknown key ids can't flood the key endpoint
takeaways.body: When a token names a key id `AccessVerifier` doesn't know, it waits for a bounded fetch and refetches at most once every 10 seconds, so a stream of bad tokens can't hammer the endpoint.

takeaways.title: `fetchImpl` now receives `init`
takeaways.body: The `fetchImpl` option on `AccessVerifier` is now called with the request `init` as a second argument so you can pass its abort signal through, and existing one-argument fetch functions keep working.

takeaways.title: `lumen-ship check parts` flags hand-made key inputs
takeaways.body: The `parts` check has a new `key-input` rule that reports a password `Input` or `InputGroupInput` in an app folder, so copied key and token entry fields show up in the check instead of slipping through.

takeaways.title: Conditional password inputs are caught too
takeaways.body: The `key-input` rule also flags an input whose type is chosen at runtime, such as `type={secret ? 'password' : 'text'}`, so a show/hide toggle does not hide a hand-rolled key field from `lumen-ship check parts`.

takeaways.title: Use `LumenConnection` for keys, tokens and secrets
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenConnection` already provides the masked value, Replace, prefix check, status, Test and Remove, and the parts guidance now says to use it for any key, token or secret field in a settings row. When you bump `@columenlabs/lumen-ship`, replace each flagged input with `LumenConnection`, or add one `key-input` line to the app's parts baseline until you do. This is not breaking, because the check only fails when the count rises above the baseline.

takeaways.title: Offer a fresh chat for new work
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, override the protected `offerFresh(input)` hook on `LumenAgent` and return `true` when a message starts new work in a long chat, and `ask()` will send a `fresh` event followed by `done` without keeping or answering the message.

takeaways.title: A fresh-chat card in the assistant
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenAssistant` now shows a card under the message asking whether to start a fresh chat, with a ＋ button to send it in a new chat and a × button to keep it in the current one.

takeaways.title: Keep a message in the current chat
takeaways.body: `AskInput.stay` and `AssistantMessage.stay` mark a message that was kept after the offer, so `offerFresh` is not run again for it, and `useAssistantChat().fresh(choice, extra)` lets you send the user's choice from your own UI.

takeaways.title: New types for the fresh offer
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types`, the new `{ kind: 'fresh' }` item and the `fresh` event let you handle the offer in a custom assistant view.

takeaways.title: Choose which own AI ways each person may use
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, the new `AssistantOptions.ownWays(caller)` returns the allowed ways (`key`, `plan`) per provider for that person, and `PUT /my-key` and `POST /my-signin(/finish)` now refuse to add a way that isn't allowed.

takeaways.title: Keep own-key payers off the shared key
takeaways.body: In `AssistantOptions`, the new `ownFallback(caller)` lets you return `false` so a person who pays with their own key first never moves to the app's shared key (the default is `true`).

takeaways.title: Keep a plan-limited turn on the same model
takeaways.body: Set `AssistantOptions.planFallback: 'shared'` and, when a person's own plan hits its usage limit mid-turn, the same model carries on using the app's shared key and that part is recorded as shared spend (`payer: 'app'`).

takeaways.title: Run safety checks on the shared key
takeaways.body: `complete({ payer: 'app' })` in `@columenlabs/lumen-ai` always runs on the shared key, whoever pays for the person's answers.

takeaways.title: Settings shows only the ways a person may use
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, Settings ▸ Model providers lists only the allowed ways and adds an "Answers run on" row once an own key or plan is set.

takeaways.title: Let the app choose each turn's tier
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `createAssistant({ pickTier: false })` makes `agentTurn` run on exactly the `input.tier` you pass, so an app can send chat to a cheap model and edits to a strong one.

takeaways.title: Cleaner assistant panel when the app routes
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenAssistant` now hides the header tier menu and the composer's `#`, `/model` and `/escalate` commands when the status reports `pick_tier: false`.

takeaways.title: Status tells the UI who picks the tier
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types`, `AssistantStatus` has a new `pick_tier` field, which is `false` when the app picks the tier, so custom assistant UIs can follow the same rule.

takeaways.title: Agents choose where their chat compacts
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, a `LumenAgent` subclass can now override the protected `compactAt()` method to return the token count past which the older part of the chat is summarized, so an app's agent can keep chats shorter than the 150k default (`COMPACT_AT`).

takeaways.title: The assistant's context bar follows the agent's limit
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenAssistant` has a new `compactAt` prop (150k by default) that moves the context bar's tick and warning colour to the limit your agent uses.

takeaways.title: Keep the model out of assistant answers
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `createAssistant` takes a new `hideModel` option (part of `AssistantOptions`) that stops the assistant from naming its model, provider or tier.

takeaways.title: No more "What model are you?" leaks
takeaways.body: The kit used to add a line telling the assistant to state its tier, model and provider when asked, placed after your own instructions, so an app could not override it. Setting `hideModel: true` in `createAssistant` removes that line.

takeaways.title: Safe by default, opt in per app
takeaways.body: `hideModel` is off by default, so existing `createAssistant` calls behave exactly as before and you only change behavior where you set it.

takeaways.title: Generate images from the server
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ai, `assistant.image(caller, { task, prompt, images?, size?, quality?, run? })` makes one image on the paying user's own key, billed and capped in the allowance like `complete`, and works from the reference `images` when you pass them.

takeaways.title: Tool images show as a card
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ui-types, the new `StepItem.image` (`{ url, alt?, cost? }`) means a tool output's `image` renders in `LumenAssistant` as a picture card with Zoom, Use as reference, Download and Make another actions.

takeaways.title: Composer modes
takeaways.body: `LumenAssistant` has a new `modes` prop that adds toggles beside the paperclip, such as Make an image. The active mode is sent with the message as `use` (`AssistantMessage.use`, `AskInput.use`) so your app's plan can read it.

takeaways.title: Progress box for slow image tools
takeaways.body: Set `LumenAssistant`'s new `imageTool` prop to your tool's name, and while that tool runs its line shows a "Making the image · Usually 10 to 20 s" box instead of a plain step.

takeaways.title: Reply to selected chat text
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant`, select text inside any single chat message and use the floating Reply bar to quote it above the composer, so the next message is sent as `AssistantMessage.quote` (`{ text, from }`).

takeaways.title: Attach images from the composer
takeaways.body: `LumenComposer` now shows a paperclip button when `images` is on, so users can pick files as well as paste or drop them.

takeaways.title: The agent reads the quote
takeaways.body: `LumenAgent.ask` from @columenlabs/lumen-ai keeps the quote in `AskMeta.quote` and gives the model a leading text part, built with the exported `quoteLead` and `quoteOf`, that names whose message was quoted.

takeaways.title: Version text that opens the notes
takeaways.body: `WhatsNew` has a new `label` prop that shows the version in the status bar and opens the release notes when clicked.

takeaways.title: A month's spend now adds up per task and model
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, the `spend:YYYY-MM` document gains an optional `tasks` list of `TaskSpend` entries, so an app's admin page can show what each kind of work costs in answers (`runs`), model calls, tokens in, cache reads, tokens out, cost and total time (`ms`).

takeaways.title: Chat and `complete` answers are tagged with their task automatically
takeaways.body: A chat answer is counted as `chat` using its turn's `ms`, and a `complete` call is counted under its `task` and timed around the call, so you don't need to change existing calls to get the per-task tally.

takeaways.title: Name a call's work with `complete({ tag })`
takeaways.body: When a task does more than one kind of work, such as a first try and a repair, pass `tag` to `complete` to count that call under a different name in the `tasks` list.

takeaways.title: `State.addSpend` takes the task and time
takeaways.body: `State.addSpend(id, payer, parts, at?)` now accepts the task and time for the tally, and the existing `rows` are written exactly as before, so current readers keep working.

takeaways.title: Per-call effort for completions
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `assistant.complete(caller, { effort })` now accepts an optional `effort`, so you can set how hard the model thinks for that one call.

takeaways.title: Effort now reaches every provider
takeaways.body: Models that previously never got an effort from `assistant.complete()` now receive your `effort` as the request's `reasoning.effort`, and `max` is sent as `high`.

takeaways.title: Call effort beats saved tier effort
takeaways.body: For models that read the person's saved tier effort (`output_config.effort`), the `effort` you pass to `assistant.complete(caller, { effort })` now wins for that call, so you can compare models at the same effort on one background job.

takeaways.title: Settings section headers line up
takeaways.body: In the Settings panel from `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, a section's description is now vertically centred with its title (`sm:items-center`) at the `sm` breakpoint and wider, instead of sitting lower than the title's icon row.

takeaways.title: Phone layout and API unchanged
takeaways.body: On phones the Settings section description still sits under the title, and no props or options changed, so an app needs no code changes to pick this up.

takeaways.title: Settings header rule documented
takeaways.body: The Settings part guide now says a section's header is one centred line drawn by the panel, so an app can rely on the panel for the header's alignment.

takeaways.title: Per-person monthly cap for the assistant
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `createAssistant({ allowance: { cap } })` now accepts an optional `cap(id)` function that returns the units one person may spend per month on the shared keys, such as their plan's allowance or an admin's override.

takeaways.title: A failing cap lookup never blocks an answer
takeaways.body: If your `cap(id)` returns nothing, returns a negative number or throws, `createAssistant` falls back to the admin's cap in Settings, so you can read plans or overrides from a database without risking the assistant's reply.

takeaways.title: No migration for existing apps
takeaways.body: Apps that don't pass `allowance.cap` keep the admin's cap exactly as before, and `period: 'once'` allowances are unchanged.

takeaways.title: Give each AI provider its own shared-key section
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui/assistant`, `assistantAdminSections` now takes an optional `providers: { id, label }[]`, so the admin Settings menu lists one sub-section per provider holding that provider's shared key instead of a single Shared model keys section.

takeaways.title: Allowance is now its own section
takeaways.body: When you pass `providers` to `assistantAdminSections`, the cap input moves into a new `assistant-shared-allowance` section that sits above the per-provider key sections.

takeaways.title: Predictable ids for the new sections
takeaways.body: Each provider's section from `assistantAdminSections` has the id `assistant-shared-key-<id>` (using the `id` you passed in `providers`) and is marked `sub: true`, so you can find or target it like any other Settings section.

takeaways.title: Settings section descriptions sit beside the title
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenSettings` now draws a section's `description` on the same baseline as its title (`Email | How the app sends mail`) from the `sm` breakpoint up, so desktop section headers are one line shorter and no prop changes are needed.

takeaways.title: Retry a failed assistant turn with one icon
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, a turn that ended in an error now shows a Retry icon (tooltip and `aria-label` "Retry") in its action row beside Copy, so users can resend it without retyping.

takeaways.title: Resend programmatically with `retry`
takeaways.body: `useAssistantChat()` now returns `retry(at, user, extra)`, which sends the failed turn's words, `@` refs, `#` tier and images again as a new message, using your app's current `extra()` for context and screen.

takeaways.title: Retried turns are marked in the thread
takeaways.body: The new message is labeled "Retry", and the old error turns grey and stops offering Retry, so the history shows which attempt is current.

takeaways.title: Types carry the retried state
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types`, the `user` and `error` chat items gain an optional `retried` field, an additive change that needs no migration.

takeaways.title: An agent answer no longer ends on a tool call
takeaways.body: In `LumenAgent` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent`, the last allowed step (by default the 8th model call, set with `plan.maxSteps`) now runs with no tools, so the agent answers in words from what it found and says what is left.

takeaways.title: New `LAST_STEP_NOTE` and `MAX_STEPS` exports
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent`, you can import `LAST_STEP_NOTE`, the text added to the instructions on the final step, and `MAX_STEPS`, the default step limit of 8, instead of hard-coding them in your app.

takeaways.title: Clearer docs for `plan.maxSteps`
takeaways.body: The `plan.maxSteps` description in `@columenlabs/lumen-ai` now says the last call has no tools, and the README has a short **Steps** paragraph on how the limit works.

takeaways.title: Assistant shows what it found on the web
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, web search steps now read "Searched the web: <query> · N results" and fold open to show linked results, with no new prop to set.

takeaways.title: Numbered Sources chips on every turn
takeaways.body: At the end of each `LumenAssistant` turn, a **Sources** row shows one numbered chip per page the assistant read, and each chip opens that page in a new tab.

takeaways.title: Web steps in the view model
takeaways.body: From @columenlabs/lumen-ui-types/assistant, `StepItem` has an optional `web` field (`StepWeb`) holding a search's `query` and `results`, a page `read`, or a failed read as `tried`, so custom renderers can show web activity too.

takeaways.title: Web steps are filled in for live and stored chats
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ai, the new `webStep()` populates `step.web` for `web__*` tools, so streamed answers and saved chats carry the same data, even when an answer is cut off.

takeaways.title: Steer a running answer
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant`, pressing Enter while an answer is running now steers your message into that answer, using `LumenAgent.steer(message)` from @columenlabs/lumen-ai, and the panel shows the line marked Steered.

takeaways.title: Queue follow-up messages
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant`, Alt+Enter queues a message, and `useAssistantChat` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui now returns `queue`, `steerQueued` and `unqueue` so you can build your own queue UI.

takeaways.title: Steer route on the adapter
takeaways.body: The new optional `AssistantAdapter.steer` calls `POST /chats/:id/steer` with `{message}` and expects `{steered}` back, and an app whose server answers 404, 405 or 410 gets a Queue-only panel.

takeaways.title: Unread steers are not lost
takeaways.body: If an answer ends before reading a steer, it comes back as an `unsteered` event and goes first in the queue, and you can set `plan.steer: false` on a model to turn steering off for it.

takeaways.title: New chat types
takeaways.body: From @columenlabs/lumen-ui-types, `AssistantEvent` gains `steered` and `unsteered`, and the user `ChatItem` gains an optional `steered` flag. The existing `queued` event is unchanged, so current code keeps working.

takeaways.title: Two-finger scroll no longer zooms chat images
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `ChatImage` now zooms only on a pinch (or Ctrl + wheel, which is how browsers report a pinch), so a trackpad two-finger scroll no longer changes the zoom level.

takeaways.title: Two-finger pan on a zoomed image
takeaways.body: `ChatImage` now turns on `trackPadPanning`, so you can pan a zoomed-in image in any direction with two fingers, while at fit in the chat panel two fingers still scroll the chat.

takeaways.title: Always-on pan in the lightbox
takeaways.body: In the `ChatImage` lightbox, the new `panAtFit` behavior lets two fingers pan the image even when it is shown at fit.

takeaways.title: Mouse wheel now pans instead of zooming
takeaways.body: A plain mouse wheel over `ChatImage` now pans the image, so if your app or its help text tells people to zoom with the wheel, change that to Ctrl + wheel, the zoom buttons or a double-click.

takeaways.title: `@` now points at things and `#` picks the tier
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the composer opens the point-at list (sources, This page, Point at…, Selected text) on `@` and the tier list on `#`, the reverse of before. No props or types changed, so your app only needs the version bump, but update any help text, docs or onboarding that tells people to type `#` to point at something or `@` to choose a tier.

takeaways.title: Chips match their trigger key
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant`, a pointed thing now shows an `@` chip and a chosen tier shows a `#` chip, both in the composer and on messages already sent.

takeaways.title: Placeholder hint shows the new keys
takeaways.body: The `LumenAssistant` composer placeholder now ends with `(/ @ #)`, listing `@` always and `#` only when your app offers more than one tier.

takeaways.title: Assistant chats by scope
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant`, the new `chatScope` prop (`{ current, label, name? }`) makes the Chats menu list only the current scope's chats, with a switch named `label` at the top to show all of them.

takeaways.title: Zoom and pan for chat images
takeaways.body: Images passed to `LumenAssistant` through `images` now open full width in the panel with wheel, pinch, drag and double-click zoom and pan, and a Full screen button opens them in a 90% lightbox.

takeaways.title: Scope on saved chats
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types`, `AssistantChatRow` has a new optional `scope` field, so you can record where a chat was started (an app's workspace, project or record) and feed it to `chatScope`.

takeaways.title: Unpickable selector rows now show why
takeaways.body: In `LumenSelector` and `LumenSelectorList` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, an option with `disabled: 'Added'` now renders dimmed with a small ✓ chip showing that string, instead of looking like a normal row that ignores clicks.

takeaways.title: Keyboard navigation skips rows that can't be picked
takeaways.body: In `LumenSelectorList`, the arrow keys and the default (Tab) row now pass over options with `disabled` set, and the Tab hint follows the highlighted row.

takeaways.title: The reason is visible without hovering
takeaways.body: In the `LumenSelector` combobox, the reason chip replaces the old tooltip wrapper, so a string passed to `LumenOption`'s `disabled` is readable at a glance. No API change: `disabled` is still `boolean | string`.

takeaways.title: Paste or drop images into assistant chats
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, set the new `images` prop on `LumenAssistant` or `LumenComposer` (off by default) and users can paste (Cmd/Ctrl+V) or drop images on the box, see them as removable thumbnail chips, and send them with their next message.

takeaways.title: Send images to the agent
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent`, `AskInput` now accepts `images`, which are checked for type, count and size and passed to the model as file parts alongside the message.

takeaways.title: Image types and limits
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types/assistant`, use `AssistantImage`, `AssistantMessage.images`, and the bounds `ASSISTANT_IMAGE_TYPES`, `ASSISTANT_IMAGES_MAX` and `ASSISTANT_IMAGE_CHARS` to type and validate image attachments in your own chat code.

takeaways.title: Usage history per person
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `State.addUsage` and `State.usage` keep one `usage:YYYY-MM` document per person, with one entry per chat or run (title, first and last use, calls, tokens in, cache read and out, USD, and parts per tier and model), and the newest 300 entries are kept.

takeaways.title: Name your background runs and chats
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `complete(caller, { run: { id, title } })` adds every call with the same run id into one line, `complete` now also returns `usage`, and `agentTurn(caller, { chat })` records the turn under `chat:<id>`.

takeaways.title: Read a month of usage over HTTP
takeaways.body: `assistantRoutes` now serves `GET /usage?month=YYYY-MM`, which returns the caller's own total, spend rows, entries and months with history, and answers 400 for a bad month.

takeaways.title: Spend per model and provider
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types`, `UsagePart` has a new optional `model` field that `Meter.part()` fills with the model id, so spend rows and history can be summed per model and provider.

takeaways.title: "This month" total in the assistant panel
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `AssistantAdapter` has a new optional `usage` method, and the panel footer now shows a This month total instead of only the open chat's cost.

takeaways.title: Longer answers from `complete()`
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `Assistant.complete()` now accepts a `maxTokens` up to the new `COMPLETE_MAX_TOKENS` export (32,000, thinking included), so an app can generate a long file in one call instead of hitting the old 8,000 cap.

takeaways.title: Know when an answer was cut
takeaways.body: The result of `Assistant.complete()` now has a `cut: boolean` field that is `true` when the model stopped at the token limit, so an app can retry or continue instead of saving a half-written answer.

takeaways.title: Streamed answers keep long requests alive
takeaways.body: `Assistant.complete()` now streams the answer from every supported provider, so a long answer keeps its connection and no longer fails as one unstreamed request.

takeaways.title: xAI is now an assistant provider
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, add `XAI_MODELS` (Grok 4.3, Grok 4.6 and Grok 4.7) to the `models` list your app passes in, and Grok models become available for completions and agent turns.

takeaways.title: Provider type includes xAI
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types/assistant`, `ASSISTANT_PROVIDERS` now includes `'xai'`, so provider-aware code and types can handle it.

takeaways.title: Key-only xAI setup
takeaways.body: `PROVIDERS.xai` in `@columenlabs/lumen-ai` (label xAI, key prefix `xai-`, link to the xAI console) lets users connect Grok by pasting an API key, with no sign-in flow.

takeaways.title: Tools used earlier in a chat stay available
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ai, with lazy tools on (more than `LAZY_AT` tools), a short follow-up like "yes" no longer fails with `AI_NoSuchToolError` when the model calls the write tool it used on the previous turn.

takeaways.title: Lazy tools remember the conversation
takeaways.body: The new `usedTools(messages)` reads the `tool-call` parts and `tool_search` results in a chat history, and `lazyTools(tools, core, groupOf, start)` switches on the latest 8 of those tools that still exist from the first step, so the model no longer has to run `tool_search` again.

takeaways.title: Prompt growth is capped at 8 tool schemas
takeaways.body: The prompt only grows by the schemas of tools the chat has already touched, and never by more than 8, so large tool sets stay lazy.

takeaways.title: Smaller font payload in every app build
takeaways.body: The `theme.css` stylesheet in `@columenlabs/lumen-ui` now declares its four font families for Latin and Latin Extended only, so an app that imports it ships 8 font files instead of 23.

takeaways.title: Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese text now uses the system font
takeaways.body: If your app renders those scripts, add your own `@font-face` rules after importing `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`'s `theme.css`, or accept the system font. Latin text is unchanged.

takeaways.title: Fonts now ship inside the kit
takeaways.body: `@columenlabs/lumen-ui` bundles the font files, with each family's license, so `theme.css` no longer relies on the separate font packages, which are dropped as dependencies.

takeaways.title: Resized columns keep numbers on the right
takeaways.body: In `LumenView` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, a column you drag to a new width with `resizable` now keeps its numeric and other non-text cells on the right edge instead of jumping to the left.

takeaways.title: Units no longer disappear after a resize
takeaways.body: In `LumenView`, a `UnitValue` in a dragged column now keeps its unit visible, where before the unit could be clipped until you double-clicked to reset the width.

takeaways.title: Capped units columns leave room for the unit
takeaways.body: In `LumenView`, the width cap on a resized column that shows units now reserves space for `--unit-slot`, so the number and its unit fit together.

takeaways.title: Lazy parts now load themselves when the tab is idle
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ui, every component made with `lazyPart` now loads on its own 8 seconds after page load, so a deploy can no longer remove a file a long-open tab still needs, with no wiring in your app.

takeaways.title: Show a fallback when a lazy part's file is gone
takeaways.body: `lazyPart` now takes a third argument, `stale`, a component that draws in place of the part when its file no longer exists after a deploy.

takeaways.title: No more page reload in the middle of a chat
takeaways.body: When a `lazyPart` has a `stale` component, `LumenBoundary` no longer reloads the page on a stale-build error, so an app's chat Markdown component can fall back to plain text and keep the conversation intact.

takeaways.title: Whole-number columns no longer show decimals
takeaways.body: In `toFrame` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, a number column whose values are all whole numbers now gets the `rounded` format, so pushed CSVs and fetched frames show `27` or `1,235` instead of `27.00`.

takeaways.title: Year columns read as plain years
takeaways.body: In `toFrame` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, a number column where every value is a year between 1900 and 2100 now gets the `integer` format, so values like `2026` stay readable as years.

takeaways.title: Decimal columns are unchanged, and saved frames keep their format
takeaways.body: `toFrame` still gives the `number` format to any column with a non-whole value, and frames already saved keep their stored format until you push or refresh them again.

takeaways.title: Chat history now reads from the prompt cache on later turns
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, the agent's `cachedTurn` now marks the message just before the newest person's message with `cacheControl`, so the chat so far is cached and the next turn can read it.

takeaways.title: Cache entries no longer go stale after one turn
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, the agent no longer relies only on the request-level breakpoint, which ended on the newest message and its per-turn bearings (`withLead`). That prefix could never match the next turn, so chats wrote the cache every turn and never read it.

takeaways.title: Instructions and tools are cached as a system message
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `cachedTurn` now sends the agent's instructions as a system message with `cacheControl`, so tools and instructions stay cached across turns without any change to your agent setup.

takeaways.title: Per-tier usage pop-up in the assistant panel
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, the usage line now opens a compact pop-up table (`UsageTable`) with one row per usage part and a Total row, so you can see where cost and tokens went.

takeaways.title: Denser usage line
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant`, the usage line (`UsageLine`) now reads `$cost · ↑in ↓out ⚡cache%` and keeps the context bar, so you get cost, token and cache numbers at a glance.

takeaways.title: Hand-off counts on usage parts
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ui-types, `UsagePart` has a new optional `runs` field, set by `UsageMeter.handOff()` in @columenlabs/lumen-ai, so you can show how many times a chat escalated to a higher tier.

takeaways.title: Show a pushed dataset as a workspace tab
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `createWorkspaces(...).frameTab(owner, workspace, { name, frame, start? })` adds a tab over a frame the person already has, so a dataset an outside agent sent with `pushFrame` can now appear in a workspace without a run or recipe.

takeaways.title: Prompt caching for assistant turns
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, the turn settings used by `LumenAgent` now always send an ephemeral cache breakpoint, so later steps and later turns of an assistant chat read the tools, instructions and earlier messages from cache at about a tenth of the input price.

takeaways.title: Lint, type-check and build now run side by side in CI
takeaways.body: In the Lumen repository's CI workflow, a pull request's three checks start together and each prints its full output when it ends, so you see every failure in one run. Locally the step took 67 s instead of 128 s.

takeaways.title: A stalled install no longer blocks CI for minutes
takeaways.body: The CI install step is now cut off at 45 s and tried once more. Before, one stalled install ran 360 s and the whole job took 437 s.

takeaways.title: Stuck CI jobs fail after 3 minutes
takeaways.body: The CI job timeout drops from 15 min to 3, so a hung run reports a failure quickly and you can re-run it.

takeaways.title: Fetch recipes for workspace tabs
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types/frames`, a tab can now use the `{kind:'fetch', requests, each?, rows?, pick?}` recipe to read from the web with `{field}` templates, with `fetchCalls` capping a run at 50 reads (`FETCH_CALLS`) and `fetchedRows` shaping the rows.

takeaways.title: Browser script runner
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `runBrowserFrame` runs a `{kind:'script', runtime:'browser', code, requests?}` tab in a sandboxed iframe, so you can wrangle fetched data in the browser and save the rows with one `PUT /frames/:id/rows`.

takeaways.title: Scripts get no network of their own
takeaways.body: Browser script code runs in a Web Worker inside an opaque-origin iframe, with a CSP of `connect-src 'none'` and a 30 s stop, and its only way out is `hub.fetch(url, {key})` through your app's `POST <api>/fetch` proxy.

takeaways.title: Pushed datasets
takeaways.body: In the workspace store, `pushFrame` replaces a tab's rows (or appends them, with an optional key), `removeFrame` deletes the tab, and `parseCsv` turns CSV text into rows (1 MB per call).

takeaways.title: Markdown tables in assistant answers
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenAssistant` now draws GitHub-style Markdown tables as real tables with the kit's table component instead of raw `| a | b |` text, with no new prop or option to set.

takeaways.title: Tables follow the kit's table rules
takeaways.body: Table rows in `LumenAssistant` answers stay on one line, long values truncate with the full text in `title`, and a wide table scrolls sideways inside its own box.

takeaways.title: Number columns line up
takeaways.body: In `LumenAssistant` answers, a column that holds only numbers now right-aligns on one edge, header included, and uses `.num` figures.

takeaways.title: Strikethrough in answers
takeaways.body: `LumenAssistant` now renders `~~text~~` as strikethrough, so assistant answers can show struck-out text.

takeaways.title: Picker option names are no longer cut off by long details
takeaways.body: In `LumenSelector` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, an option's name now keeps its natural width (up to two thirds of the row) and a long detail truncates first, so names stay whole on a phone without any new prop or change in your app.

takeaways.title: + Data lists every app recipe
takeaways.body: In the Edit widget's **+ Data** menu and the data step of Add widget, from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, every recipe passed to `WorkspacesProvider` through `recipes` now appears, grouped by its `WorkspaceRecipe.group`, even if nobody has pulled it yet and even if your app registers no catalog.

takeaways.title: Create a frame from a recipe over HTTP
takeaways.body: In @columenlabs/lumen-ai, `workspaceRoutes` now accepts `POST /frames` with `{ name, recipe }` and calls your store's `makeFrame`, which reuses a frame that already runs that recipe.

takeaways.title: Linked frames are no longer dropped
takeaways.body: `dropFrameIfUnused` now keeps any frame that a tab's config still links, so removing one widget no longer deletes data another tab depends on.

takeaways.title: Docs build log drops from 9,331 lines to 32
takeaways.body: Running `bun run build` in the docs project now prints only warnings and errors, so a contributor can read the whole output and spot a real problem.

takeaways.title: The `"use client"` notice is gone, other warnings stay
takeaways.body: The docs build's `onwarn` handler now drops only `MODULE_LEVEL_DIRECTIVE`, which printed 527 times from dependencies, so you can still see every other warning, including the chunk size one.

takeaways.title: Quiet by default, same site
takeaways.body: The docs build config now sets `logLevel: 'warn'`, which stops the per-asset listing, and the built docs site is unchanged.

takeaways.title: Icons picked by name now load as one lazy file
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the view icon loader `loadLucide` now imports the `icons` map from `lucide` in a single dynamic import, so an app that builds the kit emits one lazy icon file instead of about 1,800.

takeaways.title: Icon names match regardless of dashes and case
takeaways.body: When you give an icon name to the view icon loader in `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `arrow-down-01` and `ArrowDown01` now resolve to the same icon.

takeaways.title: Far fewer build files per app
takeaways.body: Apps that build `@columenlabs/lumen-ui` no longer risk hitting a host's asset file limit because of icons. In one app the output dropped from 1,806 files to 61, with no change to first-page JavaScript.

takeaways.title: SettingField labels use the full row when there is no control
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, a `SettingField` that has only an `end` (a switch or a `SettingStatus` pill) and no `children` now lets its label take the row, so short labels no longer cut off on a phone.

takeaways.title: The assistant can move the person's screen again
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `LumenAgent` now adds a `screen` tool to a turn when `plan.screen` is on and the message carries `screen`, so the assistant can go to a page, open settings, show a chart, open an item or point at something.

takeaways.title: Screen moves show as chips with Undo
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenAssistant` now sends the page map (`screenMapFor`) with each message and runs each new screen call once, showing it as a chip with ✓ and Undo, the reason it failed, or Go now when it is waiting.

takeaways.title: A Screen setting for each person
takeaways.body: `Assistant.agentTurn` now sets `plan.screen` from the person's new `screen` setting (`off` or `move`, Move by default), `PUT /settings` accepts it, and the status response returns it.

takeaways.title: The assistant learns what happened to its moves
takeaways.body: `AskInput.outcomes` and `AssistantMessage.outcomes` now carry the result of each screen call back to `LumenAgent`, which tells the model once, in the next turn's lead.

takeaways.title: `AssistantStatus.screen` is now required
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types/assistant`, if your app builds its own `AssistantStatus` object, add `screen: 'move'` or `screen: 'off'` to it.

takeaways.title: Host workspaces from the kit
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/workspaces`, `createWorkspaces({db, run, tables?, app?})` gives any app a workspace store over SQLite, using `doSql` for a Durable Object or `d1Sql` for D1, so `WorkspacesSection` and `WorkspacePage` no longer need a hand-built server.

takeaways.title: Create tabs from recipes
takeaways.body: `workspaceRoutes({base, owner, store, allow?})` now serves `POST /workspaces/:id/tabs` with `{name, recipe}`, which creates a tab from a recipe and runs it once.

takeaways.title: Run every tab again
takeaways.body: With `workspaceRoutes`, `POST /workspaces/:id/refresh` re-runs all tabs in a workspace one after another.

takeaways.title: Stricter writes and recipes
takeaways.body: Routes from `workspaceRoutes` accept writes only as same-origin JSON and accept only `call` recipes, so `sql` and `script` recipes are refused with a 422.

takeaways.title: Ship the tables as a migration
takeaways.body: `workspaceMigrations(tables)` returns the create-table SQL, so your store module can run it as its own migration.

takeaways.title: Connections are now settings rows
takeaways.body: In `LumenConnection` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, each way to connect (AI provider, email relay, hub credentials) is a `SettingField` row with a `SettingValue`, so you can show it next to your other settings and, with several ways, choose the active one in the new **Use** row.

takeaways.title: Clearer connection status
takeaways.body: `ConnectionBadge` now draws `SettingStatus` (Works, Failed, Not tested or Off), so you can show a connection's state the same way as any other setting.

takeaways.title: MCP servers as copyable rows
takeaways.body: In `McpSettings`, each server address is now a row with a Copy button, and the **From** picker chooses which app's connect steps show.

takeaways.title: Schedule editor matches the settings layout
takeaways.body: The `SchedulesSection` editor now lays out each setting as a label-beside-control row, with the On and Notify switches at the row end.

takeaways.title: No more double line above actions
takeaways.body: `SettingField` now draws a single divider between rows (`border-t`, none on the first row), so there is no doubled line above `SettingActions`.

takeaways.title: `assistantRoutes` no longer handles `POST /chat`
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `assistantRoutes` now answers `POST /chat` with 410 `moved`, so change any app client that still calls it to run chats on `LumenAgent`.

takeaways.title: Old `drafts` and undo routes are gone
takeaways.body: `assistantRoutes` no longer serves the `drafts` and `writes/:step/undo` routes for old chats, so remove any calls to them from your app.

takeaways.title: Chats run on `LumenAgent`
takeaways.body: From the `./agent` export of `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `LumenAgent` now runs every chat turn, and the assistant's own turn loop no longer exists.

takeaways.title: Smaller `Assistant` that still reads old chats
takeaways.body: `Assistant` keeps `agentTurn`, `runDraft`, `undoChange` and `complete`, and can still read, delete and purge chats saved by the old loop until they age out.

takeaways.title: Plan turns fall back when the plan is used up
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, a turn run through `LumenAgent` on a plan sign-in that hits its usage limit now finishes on a model from the app's other provider instead of ending in the limit error.

takeaways.title: New `planFallback` model wrapper
takeaways.body: `planFallback(primary, fallback, onSwitch)` wraps a plan-backed model and hands that call and every later call in the turn to the fallback when the plan runs out, so you can use the same rule in your own agent code.

takeaways.title: `agentTurn` sets `AgentTurnPlan.fallback` for you
takeaways.body: When a turn's key is a plan sign-in, `agentTurn` now fills in `AgentTurnPlan.fallback` with the app's smallest model from the other provider on the same payer's API key, and leaves the turn unchanged if that payer has no such key.

takeaways.title: Fallback usage is reported and priced separately
takeaways.body: After a swap, `LumenAgent` reports the fallback model's use as its own usage part (`Tier · <model>`), priced, and no longer counts it as free plan use.

takeaways.title: Think works on a plan sign-in
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent`, `planFetch` now sends `store: false` with `include: ['reasoning.encrypted_content']`, so the first Think turn on a subscription plan sign-in returns an answer instead of `Bad Request`.

takeaways.title: Earlier turns are replayed in full on a plan
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent`, `turnSettings` now sets the `store` provider option to `false` on a plan, so the SDK sends earlier turns as full items rather than references to stored responses.

takeaways.title: Plan requests match the assistant's own loop
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent`, `planFetch` now moves system and developer messages into `instructions` and drops the `$schema` tag from function parameters, so `input` holds only the conversation.

takeaways.title: Plan failures name their cause
takeaways.body: When `planFetch` gets a non-2xx response, it now logs `assistant_plan_refused` with the provider's stated reason, so you can see why a plan request was rejected.

takeaways.title: Export a server-paged table in full
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, give the `paging` prop of `LumenView` the new `all` function (`ServerPaging.all`) and the table's Export saves every matching row, not just the page on screen.

takeaways.title: Clear menu wording and a failure toast
takeaways.body: When `paging.all` is set, the Export menu entries Download CSV and Copy to clipboard read "Every matching row", and a toast tells the user if fetching the rows fails.

takeaways.title: Guidance on exporting paged tables
takeaways.body: The table part page now has an Export section with a new rule: an app should not add its own Download button beside a paged table, and should pass `paging.all` instead.

takeaways.title: Status, toggle and actions on expandable rows
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `LumenExpandRow` takes new optional `status`, `toggle` and `actions` props, so one row can show a status pill, an on/off switch that sits outside the expand button, and an action bar.

takeaways.title: One layout for every setting
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the new `SettingField`, `SettingValue`, `SettingStatus` and `SettingActions` parts let you build a Settings section with each control in one fixed place, using `end` for a per-setting switch and `stack` to put the label above the control on a phone.

takeaways.title: Health worked out for you
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `settingHealth` and `sectionHealth` compute the status for a setting or a section (the worst item wins), and the new `SettingsSectionDef.health` field shows it as a pill by the section title and a dot in the Settings list.

takeaways.title: Notifications settings rebuilt on the new parts
takeaways.body: `NotificationsSettings` channels now use the same slots, with no uppercase sub-headers, no separate "Test" rows and no trash icon for a channel that is off.

takeaways.title: Run a chat turn in the panel's own events
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `LumenAgent.ask(input, sink)` runs one agent turn and sends text, step lines, draft cards, hand-off sections, advice, errors and stop to `sink` as `AssistantEvent`s, ending with `done {id, usage}`.

takeaways.title: Answer a chat route in one call
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `askResponse(run, {signal, stop, waitUntil})` returns the streamed (SSE) response for an app's `/chat` route, and a closed request now stops the turn.

takeaways.title: Reopen a stored chat
takeaways.body: `LumenAgent.view()` returns a stored chat as the panel's `ChatItem`s, and `LumenAgent.usage()` and `LumenAgent.stop()` report token use and end a running turn.

takeaways.title: Cards and hand-offs carry what a stored chat needs
takeaways.body: A draft card's id is now its tool call's id, so a stored chat can tell how each draft or write ended, and `escalate` reports `handoff {tier, label, why, usage}` for its section.

takeaways.title: Columns button now shows whenever the columns control is on
takeaways.body: In `LumenView` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, the Columns button now appears whenever `controls.columns` is `true` (the Table default), even when the header also shows the **+** from `onAddColumn`, so you can pick columns on a wide table where the + is scrolled off screen.

takeaways.title: Per-chat MCP connectors
takeaways.body: On `LumenAgent` from @columenlabs/lumen-ai, the new `addConnector(name, url)`, `connectors()` and `removeConnector(id)` methods let a chat connect to a remote MCP server, list its connectors and remove one.

takeaways.title: Choose the access each connector gets
takeaways.body: In a turn's `plan.connectors`, an app now lists the connectors to open and sets each one to read, read + draft or read + write, and its tools appear as the group `mcp_<id>`.

takeaways.title: Lazy tool search for big toolsets
takeaways.body: Once a turn has more than `LAZY_AT` (30) tools, `LumenAgent` sends the model only the core tools plus `tool_search`, and `plan.lazy` (`{ at, core }`) lets an app change the threshold and the core set.

takeaways.title: Connector addresses are checked
takeaways.body: `addConnector` accepts only https addresses with no credentials in them (localhost is allowed while developing), and the SSRF block still applies.

takeaways.title: Export menu for tables
takeaways.body: In `LumenView`, the Download CSV button is now an Export icon button that opens a menu with Download CSV and Copy CSV, so you can save a table as a file or put it on the clipboard, and `controls.download` still turns it off.

takeaways.title: Export filtered or all rows
takeaways.body: `LumenView` has a new `allRows` prop that takes the rows before the page's filter, so while a filter hides rows the Export menu lets users choose between every matching row across all pages and the full set.

takeaways.title: Export on phones
takeaways.body: Tables in `LumenView` now put Download CSV and Copy CSV in the card's ⋯ menu on small screens, so phone users can export for the first time.

takeaways.title: Custom entries in the widget menu
takeaways.body: `LumenWidget` has a new `menu` prop that takes a `ReactNode`, so you can add your own entries to the card's ⋯ menu.

takeaways.title: Chat cards for drafts and writes
takeaways.body: In `LumenAgent` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent`, every draft and write is now stored as a card in the `lumen_cards` table, and you can list, save, dismiss or undo cards with the new `cards()`, `saveCard`, `dismissCard` and `undoCard` methods.

takeaways.title: Undo for assistant writes
takeaways.body: In `LumenAgent`, override `applyDraft` to control what Save does and `undoWrite` to control what Undo does, and the agent tells the model at the start of the next turn which cards were saved, dismissed or undone.

takeaways.title: Run drafts and undo changes as the person
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ai`, `Assistant.runDraft(caller, card)` and `undoChange(caller, card)` run a saved draft or undo a change as that person, re-check their access to the group, and stop after 60 seconds.

takeaways.title: Writes return their change
takeaways.body: In `openAiTools`, the new `wrote` hook lets a successful write return its change as well as the cut text, so your app can show an Undo card for it.

takeaways.title: Long chats compact themselves
takeaways.body: When a chat reaches 150k context tokens, the agent now compacts it with `createCompactFunction`, running the summary on the last turn's model and key and adding its cost to the next turn's usage.

takeaways.title: Plan an assistant turn for the agent runtime
takeaways.body: `Assistant.agentTurn(caller, input)` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ai` now returns `{ plan, settle }`, so you can run a turn with the person's tier, payer, tool access, instructions, page bearings and expanded slash command already worked out.

takeaways.title: Hand a task to a higher tier
takeaways.body: In the plan from `agentTurn`, `escalate` lets a higher tier run the task on the same tools, with its own usage part and the same spend cap, using the same hand-off rules as `turn`.

takeaways.title: New plan hooks on `LumenAgent`
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent`, the `LumenAgent` plan gains `lead`, `more`, `first` and `advisor`, so you can add text before the newest message, extra metered tools, a tool forced on the first step, and an advisor.

takeaways.title: Settle spend and fail clearly when nobody pays
takeaways.body: Calling `settle` adds the turn's spend to the payer's month and reports the turn and each tool call through `onStep`, while `agentTurn` throws `AssistantError` (402) when no one can pay.

takeaways.title: A chat agent base class
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent`, extend the abstract `LumenAgent` and implement `plan(turn)` (model, payer's key, effort, instructions, tool sources, money left) and `settle(end)` (outcome, usage parts, context size, time) to run one chat on the new agent runtime.

takeaways.title: Spend cap built in
takeaways.body: `LumenAgent` now stops offering tools once spend reaches the cap from `plan(turn)` and asks the model for a short answer, so a chat can't run past its budget.

takeaways.title: Models on an API key or a plan sign-in
takeaways.body: `aiModel` and `planFetch` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ai/agent` give you a model for either provider on an API key or on a plan sign-in, and `turnSettings` sets the output cap and effort in the form each provider expects.

takeaways.title: Tools at the person's access
takeaways.body: `openAiTools` turns the kit's tool groups into agent tools for one person, always offering reads, offering drafts and writes only if their access allows, and cutting each result at 16k characters.

takeaways.title: Usage priced into `UsagePart`
takeaways.body: `UsageMeter` and `tokenUsage` convert model usage, including cache reads, cache writes and reasoning tokens, into the kit's `UsagePart`, so you can meter and bill each step.

takeaways.title: Signals: warnings and errors as data
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, pass `signals` (and optional `signalOptions`) through `LumenShell bar={{ signals, signalOptions }}` or `useStatus({ signals })` to show structured warnings and errors with a level (`act`, `look` or `fyi`), a reason and a fix, instead of free-text `bar.messages`.

takeaways.title: Status chip and signals panel
takeaways.body: The new `SignalsChip` counts signals by level and shows the top one, and opening it shows `SignalsPanel`, a docked `LumenDrawer` on desktop and a bottom sheet on a phone, where users can open, mute or dismiss each signal.

takeaways.title: Signal banners
takeaways.body: Mark a `Signal` with `banner` and `SignalBanners` shows it as a banner that a user can hide for an hour with ×; signals without `banner` stay in the chip and panel.

takeaways.title: Muting and dismissing stay on the device
takeaways.body: Dismiss and mute choices are saved per app in localStorage under `lumen:signals:<app>`, a newer `at` on a signal reopens it, and repeats collapse into ×N; for an "always" mute, handle it through your own `onMute`.

takeaways.title: Status bar entries no longer overlap
takeaways.body: In `LumenShell`, status bar entries now clip instead of drawing over each other when the bar is narrow, for example with a docked drawer open.

takeaways.title: 10 rows per page for views
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ui-types/views`, `viewPageSizes` now includes 10 (`[10, 25, 50, 100, 250]`), so a view's `pagination.size` can be set to 10 and the pager size menu in `LumenPager` and the Edit widget offers "10 per page".

takeaways.title: Short cards use the view's own pager
takeaways.body: In `LumenViewCard`, set `pagination: { size: 10 }` to page a short card such as recent orders, with no hand-rolled pager beside a bare `LumenTable`.

takeaways.title: Tag chips end in an ellipsis instead of being cut mid-word
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `TagChips` in a width-capped column now shrinks each chip and ends it in an ellipsis, with the full tag shown on hover, so the last visible tag no longer reads as a broken word.

takeaways.title: `ColorChip` accepts `className` and `title`
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `ColorChip` now takes `className` to size or constrain it and `title` to show the full label on hover, and its text truncates when space runs out.

takeaways.title: More labels get icons from `tagIcon`
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `tagIcon` now recognizes doc, template, how-to, partner and link words, so tags like `Doc` and `Template` show a file, layout, bulb, handshake or link icon.

takeaways.title: Tags render as coloured chips in tables
takeaways.body: On a `ViewField` in @columenlabs/lumen-ui-types, the new `tags` option makes the table cell draw chips instead of comma text, using the field's `values` or splitting the text on commas when there are none.

takeaways.title: New `TagChips` component
takeaways.body: Import `TagChips` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui to show tags on one line anywhere, such as drawers and cards, with a `+N` chip after 3 tags whose hover lists them all.

takeaways.title: Stable tag colours and icons
takeaways.body: `tagColor(tag)` gives each tag the same colour on every page and in every app, and `tagIcon(tag)` picks an icon from the tag's words (`security`, `ai`, `data`, `favorite`, `buildout` and more). Set `color` or `iconOf` on the field to override them.

takeaways.title: New `tags-text` lint rule
takeaways.body: `lumen-ship check parts` now fails when tags or labels are joined into comma text on a line that has no `tags: true`, so tag lists keep using chips.

takeaways.title: Phone bottom tab bar for the shell
takeaways.body: In `LumenShell` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the new `tabs` prop (a `NavItem[]`) shows a bottom tab bar on phones with the first four pages plus a More tab that opens the sidebar sheet, and apps that don't pass it are unchanged.

takeaways.title: Standalone `LumenTabBar`
takeaways.body: `@columenlabs/lumen-ui` now exports `LumenTabBar`, whose active tab is the closest route match, the same rule the sidebar uses.

takeaways.title: Status bar and safe area handle the tab bar
takeaways.body: While a tab bar is showing, the shell sets `--shell-tabbar-offset` so the status bar sits above it, and the tab bar adds safe-area padding at the bottom of the screen.

takeaways.title: Split notification settings in two
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, the new `parts` prop on `NotificationsSettings` takes `'all'` (default), `'channels'` (email, ntfy and webhooks only) or `'events'` (only the events × channels grid), so an app can show what is sent and where it goes in separate Settings sections.

takeaways.title: Group notification events under a label
takeaways.body: Set the new `group` field on a `NotifyEvent` passed to `NotificationsSettings`, and events sharing a group are listed under that group's label, such as "Limits" or "Watchdog".

takeaways.title: One line per event row
takeaways.body: In `NotificationsSettings`, each event row now shows its label followed by the detail cut off with an ellipsis, and hovering shows the full text, so long lists are easier to scan.

takeaways.title: Checkbox columns stay visible on phones
takeaways.body: On small screens, the detail text in `NotificationsSettings` event rows moves into the hover, so the channel checkbox columns stay in view.

takeaways.title: Resizable table columns
takeaways.body: In `@columenlabs/lumen-ui`, `configureLumen({ resizableColumns: true })` lets users resize columns on every table in an app, and the `resizable` prop on a single `LumenView` or `LumenTable` overrides that setting for one table (off by default).

takeaways.title: Column widths kept per table
takeaways.body: Widths a user drags are now saved on their device for each table, so a resized table keeps its layout after a reload.

takeaways.title: Keyboard-friendly column grips
takeaways.body: The new `ColumnResizer` grip (`role="separator"`) on each header's right edge resizes by drag or with ← → in 16px steps, and double-click, Enter or Delete resets the column.

takeaways.title: Dragged widths can narrow long columns
takeaways.body: With `resizable` on, a dragged width caps that column's cells, so a long name column can be made narrower, with an ellipsis and the full text on hover.

takeaways.title: Simulated day for sanity runs
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ship/behavior`, `simClock()` installs a global `Date` that your sanity run moves forward, so you can replay a full day of an app's activity in seconds instead of real time.

takeaways.title: Alarms kept by the run
takeaways.body: From `@columenlabs/lumen-ship/behavior`, `SimAlarms` holds each store's alarm in the run instead of the runtime, so a simulated day schedules and fires wakes without waiting on real timers.

takeaways.title: One set of vital signs for every store
takeaways.body: `judge(wakes, { from, to, stopped }, limits?)` from `@columenlabs/lumen-ship/behavior` checks every store against the same vital signs and returns `numbers` and `broken`, so a wake loop, a runaway read or stuck work fails the check without a test written for that bug.

takeaways.title: Tunable defaults
takeaways.body: The `VITALS` export from `@columenlabs/lumen-ship/behavior` holds the default limits, tuned for a small personal system, and you can pass your own `limits` as the third argument to `judge` when your app needs different ones.

takeaways.title: Clicking a row no longer shifts a wide table sideways
takeaways.body: In `LumenView` from @columenlabs/lumen-ui, setting `openKey` and clicking a row now scrolls the table only up or down as needed, so the first column stays in view beside a docked drawer.

takeaways.title: Up/down keys keep the horizontal scroll position
takeaways.body: When you move the open row with the arrow keys in a `LumenView` that uses `openKey`, the focus call now passes `preventScroll`, so the table no longer slides sideways on each keypress.

takeaways.title: Paging to the open row keeps the sideways scroll
